content.value_statement: Vue 3 APIs and component patterns can be difficult to apply consistently. This skill provides focused guidance for typed Composition API development.
actual_capabilities: Creates Vue single-file components using TypeScript and script setup.
Defines typed props, emits, models, slots, options, and exposed component APIs.
Applies refs, computed state, watchers, effect scopes, and lifecycle hooks.
Designs composables that accept reactive inputs and return destructurable refs.
Uses Transition, Teleport, Suspense, KeepAlive, and custom directives.
limitations: Guidance targets Vue 3.5 and may not match older Vue releases.
It does not cover Options API as a preferred implementation style.
It provides patterns, but it does not run builds, tests, or browser checks independently.
It does not cover routing, state management libraries, or backend integration in depth.

use_cases.title: Create Typed Components
use_cases.description: Build maintainable single-file components with typed props, events, models, and slots.
use_cases.target_user: Frontend developers starting a Vue 3 feature

use_cases.title: Refactor Vue Logic
use_cases.description: Move component state and side effects into clear Composition API patterns and reusable composables.
use_cases.target_user: Engineers modernizing an existing Vue codebase

use_cases.title: Review Advanced Components
use_cases.description: Check transitions, teleports, suspense boundaries, caching, directives, and watcher cleanup against documented Vue patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Vue 3 component for [feature]. Use TypeScript, script setup, typed props, and clear emitted events.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a small component with established project conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Add Reactive Behavior
prompt_templates.prompt: Add computed state and watchers to this Vue component. Explain source selection, cleanup, and flush timing where relevant.
prompt_templates.scenario: Implement derived state and controlled side effects.

prompt_templates.title: Extract a Composable
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this stateful Vue logic into a typed composable. Accept reactive inputs, normalize them safely, and return destructurable refs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Reuse component logic across multiple views.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Advanced Interaction
prompt_templates.prompt: Design [interaction] with suitable Vue built-ins. Evaluate Transition, Teleport, Suspense, KeepAlive, directives, lifecycle cleanup, and accessibility requirements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan a complex component workflow and justify architectural choices.

output_examples.input: Create a typed search field with two-way binding and a submit event.
output_examples.output: A Vue component plan with a typed model, a named submit event, normalized input handling, and clear parent usage.

output_examples.input: Refactor repeated pointer tracking from three components.
output_examples.output: A reusable composable design with reactive coordinates, mounted listeners, unmounted cleanup, and stable destructuring behavior.

output_examples.input: Review a modal that renders inside an overflowing panel.
output_examples.output: A review recommending Teleport for placement, Transition for visibility changes, lifecycle cleanup, focus handling, and an accessible close flow.

best_practices: Provide the Vue version, component requirements, and relevant project conventions.
Request TypeScript types for component contracts and composable inputs.
Verify generated patterns with project tests, linting, and browser behavior.
anti_patterns: Do not request deep reactivity when value replacement is sufficient.
Do not use watchers for state that can be expressed as computed values.
Do not expose complete component internals when a narrow public API is enough.

faq.question: Which Vue version does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets Vue 3.5 and highlights features introduced in Vue 3.3 and Vue 3.4.

faq.question: Does it support the Options API?
faq.answer: The references focus on Composition API with TypeScript and script setup.

faq.question: Can it create typed component contracts?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers typed props, events, models, slots, generic components, and explicitly exposed APIs.

faq.question: Does it help build reusable composables?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents reactive inputs, value normalization, effect cleanup, lifecycle handling, and destructurable return values.

faq.question: Which built-in components are covered?
faq.answer: It covers Transition, TransitionGroup, Teleport, Suspense, and KeepAlive, plus selected built-in directives.

faq.question: Does it test generated Vue code?
faq.answer: No. Users should run their project tests, type checker, linter, and browser checks after applying the guidance.
